info.title: DSS API
info.description:
Internal REST API for communication between the DropNext monolith and the DSS.

**Formal specification.** This API has an OpenAPIv3 specification. This means its endpoints,
query parameters, payloads, authentication scheme and webhooks are formally described in the
[OpenAPIv3 spec of the DSS API](/admin-portal/development/api-specs/v1/shopify-service/openapi.json),
which an admin can download from the admin portal.
This specification is used to generate this documentation page.
A script fetches it from `/api/shopify-service/v1/openapi.json` with the DSS's key, like every other endpoint
(see *Authentication*). The monolith's `renderDssOpenApi` Gradle task writes the same document without a running
monolith; that is how the DSS refreshes its checked-in copy.
You can also use it to [generate an API client](https://openapi-generator.tech/docs/generators/).

**Authentication.** Every request carries the DSS's key as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
The token is the value of `DSS_TO_MONOLITH_API_KEY`, one static secret that the monolith and the DSS both hold.
The monolith compares it in constant time with its own copy.
There is no token table: nothing is issued, and nothing is revoked but the one value.

**The token identifies no store.** A supplier API token names its supplier; this key names only "the DSS".
So every request says which store it is about: that is why `/stores`, `/product-variants` and `/orders` all
require a `shopify_subdomain`, as a query parameter or in the body.

**Rotation is a deploy on both sides.** The value changes in both services' secrets.
A request made while only one side has the new value is answered `401`,
which the DSS takes as a refusal rather than a transient failure: it does not retry it.

post.description:
Create a new Shopify order in the monolith. Called by the DSS when it receives
a new order webhook from Shopify. Orders are treated as immutable for now; later changes go
through a separate tickets/disputes flow. Lines without an active quotation for the
retailer/region/variant triple are persisted on the order but omitted from supplier orders.

Money amounts (`total_as_string`, `snapshot_of_price_as_string`) are decimal strings exactly
as Shopify's APIs emit them: a dot decimal separator, no thousands separators, no currency
symbol (e.g. `"109.97"`). They must be non-negative; an amount finer than the order's
`currency` allows (e.g. more than two decimals for EUR, any decimals for JPY) is rounded
half-up to the currency's minor unit.

A line's `snapshot_of_variant_title` is the variant's own title as Shopify recorded it at order time (`Small -
Blue`), or Shopify's combined product and variant name when the line has none.

`shipping_address.country_code` is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the country, as Shopify gives it.
Any other code, one of our shipping region codes included, is refused with a `400`.
The order's shipping region is the narrowest the address determines. Where its country has
regions within it, the monolith reads `zip`, and `province_code` when the postal code settles nothing
(`99501` is `US-AK`, a `BT` postal code is `UK-NI`, `35…` is `ES-CI`). Quotations are matched from
that region up to the widest region of the country.

`email` is the buyer's e-mail address as Shopify has it on the order. It is optional and
nullable: an order without a customer (e.g. a POS sale) has none. It is protected customer
data in Shopify's terms, so it is stored with the order and never logged. It is not validated
(Shopify is the source of truth); a blank value is stored as absent.

A line is not the reason an order is refused. A line naming a variant the store has not
mirrored yet is stored against a pending variant, which a background job fills in from
Shopify (through the DSS's `products/fetch`) before the order is matched. That needs the
line's `shopify_product_id`: optional and nullable, so an older DSS still decodes, but a
line naming an unknown variant without it is dropped. So is a line naming a variant of
another store. Only an order whose lines are all dropped is refused, with a `400`: there
would be nothing to store. A `financial_status` the monolith does not know is stored as it
came, with the payment state `Pending`.

A `200 OK` response means the order has been **durably persisted and queued for
asynchronous processing** — not that supplier orders or balance transactions have
been written yet. The downstream supplier-order planning, balance check, etc.,
are performed by an internal background job.

example.error: Validation error (e.g. missing fields, an unsupported currency, no shipping address, an unknown country code, no storable line).

delete.summary: Delete the variants of a product
delete.description:
Soft-delete every variant of a product that no longer exists in Shopify. Called by the DSS
on a `products/delete` webhook, which carries only the product's Shopify id. A product
unknown to the store, or one whose variants are already soft-deleted, answers `deleted: 0`.

The product is named by the `shopify_subdomain` and `product_id`
query parameters; a body on a `DELETE` has no defined meaning, so none is read.

parameters.name: shopify_subdomain
parameters.description: The Shopify subdomain identifying the store

parameters.name: product_id
parameters.description: The Shopify id of the deleted product

example.error: Store not found.

get.summary: List known Shopify variant IDs for a store
get.description:
List all Shopify variant IDs the monolith knows about for the store identified by
`shopify_subdomain`. Used by the DSS to diff against the
live Shopify catalog. Soft-deleted variants are included (the DSS needs to see them to
avoid re-creating them). Pending variants, which an order named before the catalog held
them, are left out: the monolith knows nothing of them but their id.

parameters.name: shopify_subdomain
parameters.description: The Shopify subdomain identifying the store

example.error: Store not found.

post.summary: Bulk create or update product variants
post.description:
Upsert product variants identified by their Shopify variant ID. The fields delivered
from Shopify are considered immutable in the monolith's portal UIs. The whole batch
runs in a single transaction (all-or-nothing). Returns the number of rows affected.

With `product_variants_complete: true` the batch replaces the variant set of each product
it names: the store's other variants of those products are soft-deleted, and `deleted`
counts them. Send it only when the batch holds every variant Shopify has of those products.
Absent, `null` or `false`, the batch only adds and updates, and `deleted` is `0`.

`price_as_string` is the decimal string Shopify's APIs emit: a dot decimal separator, no
thousands separators, no currency symbol (e.g. `"10.00"`). It must be non-negative; an amount
finer than `price_currency` allows is rounded half-up to the currency's minor unit.

example.error: Empty variants list.
Store not found.

409.description: A variant is already registered under a different store.

example.error: A variant is already registered under a different store.

get.summary: Look up a store by Shopify subdomain
get.description:
Look up a store known to the monolith by its Shopify subdomain
(e.g. `shopify_subdomain=acme-apparel`).

example.error: Store not found.

put.summary: Set the Shopify access token for a store
put.description:
Called by the DSS after a successful app install to persist the store's
`shopify_shop_id` and Shopify access token `api_key`. If the store already has a
`shopify_shop_id` that differs from the request, the update is rejected to protect against
overwriting another shop's token via a subdomain collision. A null `shopify_shop_id` (the DSS
could not learn it from Shopify) keeps the stored id and only replaces the token; a store that
has no id yet is then answered as not found, because a token cannot be stored without one.

An install sends `granted_access_scopes` and `missing_access_scopes` too: the grant it got against the scopes it
asked for. The monolith records it as the store's Shopify status, which clears the store's "reconnect needed"
flag when nothing is missing (and queues the shipment syncs refused meanwhile again), or sets it, and notifies
the retailer's users, when something is. Without both lists the status is left as it is.

example.error: Store not found.

post.summary: Report that Shopify refused the DSS for a store
post.description:
Sent by the DSS the moment Shopify answers it with a rejected token (`token_rejected`, an uninstalled app or a
revoked token) or with a missing access scope (`access_scope_missing`, the app asks for a scope the grant lacks),
whatever the DSS was doing for the store. Either needs the merchant to open the install link.

The monolith flags the store, keeps when that started, and notifies the retailer's users who manage stores. A
scope reason names every scope known to be lacking: the ones this and earlier reports named, and the ones the
last install or status check found missing. Only a report that tells the users something new notifies, and is
answered `first_report: true`: one that flags the store, turns its reason from the token to the scopes or back,
or names a scope they were not told of yet. The same report again (Shopify redelivers a webhook up to eight
times) is `false`, as is one naming a subset of what they were told, whichever route of the DSS it came from.

A report about a token the monolith no longer holds is answered `first_report: false` and not recorded: the
merchant reinstalled after the failure was seen, and the newer fact stands. `token_fingerprint` says which token
the report is about: the first 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters of the SHA-256 of the token's UTF-8 bytes.
Without it, the report is judged by `observed_at` instead: one observed before the last install or status check
the monolith recorded is not recorded.

Only the values of `missing_access_scopes` that read as scope handles (`read_…`, `write_…`,
`unauthenticated_…`) are kept.

400.description: `observed_at` is not an ISO 8601 point in time.

example.error: `observed_at` is not an ISO 8601 point in time.
Store not found.

post.summary: Sync DropNext shipments with Shopify fulfillments
post.description:
Sent whenever the shipments of a Shopify order change: a supplier creates one, splits a
supplier order over its tracking numbers, retires a package, or corrects a tracking number.

The request carries the whole state of the order: every live shipment, and the tracking
numbers of the retired ones. The DSS reconciles the order's fulfillments with it: it cancels
a fulfillment that carries a retired number and matches no live shipment, and creates a
fulfillment for every live shipment that has none and fits whole into what the order has
open. A shipment that does not fit is reported, not refused; it is sent again with every
later request, so it becomes a fulfillment once there is room.

**Authentication.** DropNext sends this request with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token is the value of `MONOLITH_TO_DSS_API_KEY`: a secret of its own, not the key the DSS presents when it calls the monolith. The DSS verifies it and answers `401` when it does not match.

This is sent to `<DSS_BASE_URL>/sync-shipments-with-fulfillments`

example.error: The request does not validate.

example.error: The shop has no Shopify Admin token.

example.error: Shopify refused: the app's grant on this shop lacks the access scope(s) write_merchant_managed_fulfillment_orders; re-authorize the app

get.description:
Sent when the monolith wants to know what a shop actually holds, so it can compare that with what it has
mirrored and repair the difference. The DSS reads every variant Shopify has for the shop, grouped under its
product, paging and pacing itself against the shop's rate budget.

The answer is complete or the call fails: there is no cursor and no "stopped early" flag, because the
monolith soft-deletes every variant the answer omits. A large catalog can take minutes, so this is called
from a background job and never from a request someone is waiting on.

**Authentication.** DropNext sends this request with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token is the value of `MONOLITH_TO_DSS_API_KEY`: a secret of its own, not the key the DSS presents when it calls the monolith. The DSS verifies it and answers `401` when it does not match.

This is sent to `<DSS_BASE_URL>/products/catalog?shop=<subdomain>`

parameters.name: shop
parameters.description: The Shopify subdomain of the shop to read (e.g. "acme-apparel")

401.description: The shop has no Shopify Admin token, or Shopify refused it: the app has to be installed again.

example.error: The shop has no Shopify Admin token, or Shopify refused it: the app has to be installed again.

403.description: The app's grant on the shop lacks an access scope; the message names it. The app has to be re-authorized.

example.error: The app's grant on the shop lacks an access scope; the message names it. The app has to be re-authorized.

429.description: Shopify throttled the shop; retry after `retry_after_seconds`.

example.error: Shopify throttled this shop.

post.summary: Fetch the named products as product variant items
post.description:
Sent when the monolith needs the full data of specific products: a batch of a catalog repair, or the one or
two products behind an order line whose variant was never mirrored. The DSS answers the variant items that
`POST /product-variants` already takes, so the answer can be stored as it arrives.

A product Shopify no longer has is not an error; its id comes back under `missing_product_ids` and the
monolith soft-deletes the variants it holds under it. Every product is answered whole or not at all: the
DSS paces itself against the shop's rate budget and may stop early, and then the products it did not get to
come back under `unfetched_product_ids`, to be asked for again after `next_request_after_seconds`. A call
that could answer none of the products fails instead (a `429` when Shopify throttled the shop).

**Authentication.** DropNext sends this request with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token is the value of `MONOLITH_TO_DSS_API_KEY`: a secret of its own, not the key the DSS presents when it calls the monolith. The DSS verifies it and answers `401` when it does not match.

This is sent to `<DSS_BASE_URL>/products/fetch`

get.description:
Sent when the monolith wants to know whether a store's installation of the DropNext app still works: whether
          its Admin token resolves, which of the access scopes the install asks for its grant lacks, and, per webhook
          topic the DSS handles, what Shopify is subscribed to at the DSS's callback URL (Shopify removes a subscription
          whose deliveries kept failing for a day). Read-only: it costs one monolith lookup and two Shopify queries.

          **Statuses.** `access_scopes.status` is `complete`, `missing`, or `unknown` when Shopify could not list the grant.
A topic row's `status` is `active`, `mismatched` or `missing` after a check, and after a registration also
`added`, `updated`, `repointed`, `not_applied` or `failed`. An obsolete row's `status` is `obsolete`, and after a
registration `deleted` or `delete_failed`.

          **Authentication.** DropNext sends this request with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token is the value of `MONOLITH_TO_DSS_API_KEY`: a secret of its own, not the key the DSS presents when it calls the monolith. The DSS verifies it and answers `401` when it does not match.

          This is sent to `<DSS_BASE_URL>/stores/shopify-status?shopify_subdomain=<subdomain>`

parameters.name: shopify_subdomain
parameters.description: The Shopify subdomain of the shop to check (e.g. "acme-apparel")

400.description: The subdomain is not a Shopify subdomain.

example.error: The subdomain is not a Shopify subdomain.

401.description: The shop has no Shopify Admin token, or Shopify refused it: the app has to be installed again. `code` is `shopify_token_missing` when the DSS holds no token, `shopify_token_rejected` when Shopify rejected the one it holds.

example.error: Shopify rejected the Admin token held for the shop: the app has to be installed again.

post.description:
Sent when the monolith wants a store's webhook subscriptions brought to what the DSS handles, the way an
          install registers them, without the merchant: it adds the missing topics, updates and repoints the ones that
          deliver otherwise or elsewhere, and deletes the ones at the DSS's callback URL for a topic it does not handle.
          It changes the shop's subscriptions, never its token. Running it twice changes nothing the first run left
          right. A topic Shopify refused is a `failed` row, not the status of the call.

          **Statuses.** `access_scopes.status` is `complete`, `missing`, or `unknown` when Shopify could not list the grant.
A topic row's `status` is `active`, `mismatched` or `missing` after a check, and after a registration also
`added`, `updated`, `repointed`, `not_applied` or `failed`. An obsolete row's `status` is `obsolete`, and after a
registration `deleted` or `delete_failed`.

          **Authentication.** DropNext sends this request with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token is the value of `MONOLITH_TO_DSS_API_KEY`: a secret of its own, not the key the DSS presents when it calls the monolith. The DSS verifies it and answers `401` when it does not match.

          This is sent to `<DSS_BASE_URL>/stores/shopify-webhooks/register`

post.summary: Push a tracking status update to Shopify
post.description:
Sent when the monolith receives a tracking status update (via the Ship24 webhook).
The DSS should create a FulfillmentEvent in Shopify and return its ID.

A `401` or a `403` is not retried. Once the store is re-authorized, the monolith sends the newest checkpoint of
each shipment that got one meanwhile again, so Shopify ends on the current status. A checkpoint sent before
adds no second event: the DSS reuses an event with the same status and time.

**Authentication.** DropNext sends this request with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token is the value of `MONOLITH_TO_DSS_API_KEY`: a secret of its own, not the key the DSS presents when it calls the monolith. The DSS verifies it and answers `401` when it does not match.

This is sent to `<DSS_BASE_URL>/tracking-update`
